question: The most common isotopes used in a nuclear weapon are of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uranium and plutonium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Uranium-235** and **Plutonium-239** are the most common isotopes used in nuclear weapons.
 
• Uranium-235 is highly fissile, making it suitable for use in nuclear reactors and weapons.
 
• Plutonium-239 is produced in nuclear reactors from Uranium-238 and is also fissile.
 
• These isotopes undergo nuclear fission, a process that releases a tremendous amount of energy used in nuclear explosions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes:**

 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a particular chemical element which differ in neutron number, and consequently in nucleon number.
 
• All isotopes of a given element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in each atom.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Fission:**
 
 
• Nuclear fission is a reaction in which the nucleus of an atom splits into two or more smaller nuclei, along with the release of energy.
 
• This process is used in nuclear reactors and nuclear weapons.
 
• Fission of heavy elements such as Uranium-235 and Plutonium-239 releases a large amount of energy.
 
 
 
• **Uranium-235:**
 
 
• Uranium-235 is an isotope of uranium making up about 0.72% of natural uranium.
 
• Unlike the predominant isotope uranium-238, it is fissile, meaning it can sustain a chain reaction of nuclear fission.
 
 
 
• **Plutonium-239:**
 
 
• Plutonium-239 is an isotope of plutonium.
 
• It is a key fissile isotope used in the production of nuclear weapons and in some nuclear reactors.
 
• It is produced by exposing uranium-238 to neutron radiation in a reactor.
